reason: Pinned spec and host code verify the newline/no-trailing-bytes tension and trim-based divergence, and additive framing vectors would close a real interop gap.
The JSON Schema integer wording and JS/Rust validator behavior are verified and can produce opposite decisions from the same bytes.
The spec says kill the process while the reference architecture is multiprocess, and the JS/Rust host divergence is concrete though process-tree fixes are somewhat platform-sensitive.
The cited write-before-wait pattern and lack of stdin-write timeout coverage expose a plausible host hang that a bounded vector can test.
Pinned §8 text and both reference hosts confirm host nonce mode can authorize a bare allow without any durable nonce reservation.
The schema leaves retain_until unconstrained while host retention depends on it, making a past-retention replay window plausible in production stores.
This is a well-evidenced vector gap showing the timeout budget is not proven to cover a blocking stdin write.
The Binding v2 MUSTs are verified in the spec and reference verifier, but the external_verifier vector set has no corresponding IO-boundary coverage.
The request envelope lacks concrete action binding, but the proposed intent_hash semantics need tighter canonicalization and verifier-support design.
The no-third-verdict facts are verified, but safety severity is limited because unknown verdicts already fail closed.
The closed verdict schema supports the claim, but durable receipt linkage is mostly informative positioning rather than a direct interop failure.
The detail.sdk_code pathway exists, but the proposed four-cause public run record is not yet shown by one pinned command.
The draft and v1 spec depend on a stdout bound without defining its value, and a prose-only clarification is bounded and high impact.
The stale 0.5.0 independent-implementation listing is verified and directly affects RFC 7942 readiness for the current 0.6.0 suite.
The uppercase non-BCP14 FORBIDDEN usage and unresolved RSD requirements are verified draft hygiene issues with an easy -02 prose fix.
The repo-relative citations and pseudocode precedence mismatch are real, but the direct interop/safety severity is below promotion threshold.
The MCP proxy and policy-hook fit is plausible, but the repo-specific auth-gap claim was not reconciled locally and there is no warm channel.
AuthZEN COAZ/AARP has strong standards momentum at the MCP authorization boundary, while EVC has a credible adapter counter-position.
AIP overlaps the decision boundary, but its near-expiry -00 status keeps momentum and adoption risk modest.
A pinned requirement-to-vector mapping is feasible and would create useful reviewer-facing evidence for an active architecture draft.
Re-running the only independent host against vector set 0.6.0 is highly demanded evidence despite external clone/npm setup cost.
The runner can emit per-host reports and a failure_class diff would strengthen the two-reference-host implementation-status claim.
Cold-verifying the npm tarball, manifest hashes, attestation, and empty-dir run directly supports registry-closure scoring.
The spec has a clear stderr MUST NOT parse rule and the fixture set contains no stderr writer, making this an easy high-coverage vector.
